(a) 'epic-ready renders "not sharded"': epic-ready renders 'Sharding is not applied to epic-ready reviews; see the child task-done and pr-ready packs.' (internal/epicready/review.go:500). The literal 'not sharded' comes from internal/contextprofile/shards.go:266 (the unsharded Context Shard Plan body, for task-done and pr-ready) and internal/reviewmanifest/manifest.go:313 (the unsharded manifest-hash text) - both task-done/pr-ready surfaces, so the sentence attaches the string to the wrong scope. (b) 'Task-done and PR-ready add a Context Shard Plan and prompt packs when the branch diff exceeds the review context limit' - the Context Shard Plan section is rendered unconditionally for those scopes and reads 'Not sharded.' below the limit; only the plan rows and the prompt packs are conditional. A reader searching the pack for 'not sharded' will look under the wrong gate.

findings.note: internal/fsm/run/fold_test.go:118 - the 'nil-free JSON' assertion can never fire. It is `if strings.Contains(js, "null") && !strings.Contains(js, `"prev_unfixed":null`)`, and the same test already asserts s.PrevUnfixed == nil at line 106, so the snapshot always serialises prev_unfixed as null and the second conjunct is always false. Any future null elsewhere in the snapshot JSON (a container regressing to nil, a new pointer field) passes silently. Confirmed by probe: the happy-path snapshot currently contains exactly one null. Strip the known key before scanning, e.g. `strings.Contains(strings.Replace(js, `"prev_unfixed":null`, "", 1), "null")`. The four explicit container checks at line 121 partially cover the intent, which is why this is not blocking.

findings.note: internal/fsm/run/fold.go:59,78 - Fold validates that ev.At is non-zero but never that it is non-decreasing across the chain, and fold_test.go has no row for it (TestFoldSequenceInvariants:537 covers version, first-not-init, second-init, seq gap, unknown type, bad payload and the state/iter/at-zero stamps only). TestFoldNoOps demonstrates the gap incidentally: it transplants a ~20-event log into a fresh Builder at fold_test.go:513-515, so the appended events carry timestamps seconds *earlier* than the events they follow, and Fold accepts the log. For an append-only audit chain whose whole purpose is tamper evidence, a rewound clock should either be rejected or explicitly documented as out of scope. No spec text currently requires monotonicity, so this is a gap to decide rather than a contract violation.
